meanings.note: only when answering or making a phone call

examples.text: Алло, Вика, ты сейчас где находишься?
examples.trans: Hello, Vika, where are you right now?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лышать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to hear', forming an aspectual pair with 'услышать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to hear about') (слышать о + prepositional) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Как странно, я ничего об этом не слышал.
examples.trans: How strange, I've heard nothing about it.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('? = really?, oh yeah?') (disbelief) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('I have') (possession) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('from (ask from someone)') (просить у кого) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лучиться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to happen', forming an aspectual pair with 'случаться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.text: Марина, я вам обещаю: со стеной ничего не случится.
examples.trans: Marina, I promise you: nothing will happen to the wall.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: 'будут проблемы' = there'll be trouble

examples.trans: I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'говорить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to have a talk', forming an aspectual pair with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to want', forming an aspectual pair with 'захотеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('she') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'seriously'.
Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'but', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'just'.
Secondary conversational sense ('easy') (это просто = it's easy) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

развернуться.gloss: to turn around; to expand, get going

meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'вернуться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to turn around; to expand, get going', paired with 'разворачиваться'.

meanings.en: to expand, spread one's wings, build up a business
meanings.note: Secondary conversational sense ('to expand, spread one's wings, build up a business') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Если бы меня не душили люди из мэрии! Я бы тут развернулся.
examples.trans: If only the people from City Hall weren't strangling me! I would really expand here.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

уйти.gloss: to leave, to go away (on foot)

meanings.en: to leave, to go away, to walk out
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to leave, to go away (on foot)', paired with 'уходить'.
hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('oh come on!') (ну, папа!) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: возвращаться домой = to come back home; к + dative = to someone

examples.text: Запомните: зло всегда возвращается к правителю.
examples.trans: Remember: evil always comes back to the ruler.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ратно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Afterwards I'll drive you back for free.

examples.text: Вот это дело! Потом обратно бесплатно отвезу.
examples.trans: Now we're talking! Afterwards I'll drive you back for free.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).
Secondary conversational sense ('cuisine, cooking') (русская кухня = Russian cuisine) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('that') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
in 'то, что ...' = 'what, the thing that'
Declinable neuter noun meaning 'matter', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('matter, business') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('case (in court)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'can', forming an aspectual pair with 'смочь'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'why'.

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to come', forming an aspectual pair with 'приходить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'that's why'.
Secondary conversational sense ('that's why') (потому и = that's exactly why) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я устал, потому что много работал.
examples.trans: I'm tired because I worked a lot.
I'm at home because I'm ill.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'терять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to lose', paired with 'терять'.

examples.text: Что смотрите, бандерлоги? Вы совсем страх потеряли?
examples.trans: What are you staring at, you monkeys? Have you lost all fear?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('small, little').
Declinable masculine noun meaning 'key', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: The white one? Give me the keys.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('what') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see
Secondary conversational sense ('still, yet') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('even (with comparatives)') (ещё больше = even more) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.en: urgently, right away; predicative: it is urgent
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to make a phone call urgently.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, это срочно! Я должна вам сказать.
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent! I must tell you.

выходить.gloss: to go out, to get out

meanings.en: to go out, to come out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go out, to get out', paired with 'выйти'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to get out (of prison, arrest)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm going out in a minute.

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

examples.text: Давай быстрее выходи из подсобки, начинается вечерняя смена!
examples.trans: Come on out of the storage room quickly, the evening shift is starting!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'to' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: на улице = out on the street / outside
на улице холодно = it's cold outside

examples.text: На Московской улице перевернули ящики с мусором.
examples.trans: On Moskovskaya Street someone tipped over the rubbish bins.
There are reporters out on the street!

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('all right') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to wait', forming an aspectual pair with 'подождать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to expect') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: там такие деньги = there's so much money in it

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.
